claims.says: A ballpoint pen writes with a small metal ball at its tip that rolls freely across the paper (balls are about 0.3 to 1.6 mm across).
The ink sits in a thin tube, the refill; ballpoint ink is a thick, oil-based paste.
The ball is held in a socket in the metal tip, a tiny cup that holds it in place but lets it rotate.
Ink channels carry ink to the ball; as the ball rotates, ink coats it inside the socket and the rolling ball lays the ink on the paper as a thin line.
Gravity pulls the ink down to the ball; held upside down, gravity pulls the ink away from the tip, the ball runs dry and most ballpoints stop writing.
